title: Chicago is now one flight away! PAL launches nonstop service from Manila

 Chicago is now one flight away! PAL launches nonstop service from Manila 
 Philippine Airlines (PAL) launched its first nonstop service between Manila and Chicago on Nov. 9, opening a direct air link to the U.S. Midwest and offering travelers an alternative to connecting flights.
 November 11, 2026 • 
 1:59 PM 
 Share
 Philippine Airlines (PAL) launched its first nonstop service between Manila and Chicago on Nov. 9, opening a direct air link to the U.S. Midwest and offering travelers an alternative to connecting flights.
 The thrice-weekly service makes Chicago the flag carrier’s eighth destination in the United States and its territories, expanding its reach into a major economic region with a sizable Filipino-American community.
 “For Philippine Airlines, this is a strategic addition to our North American network. It expands our presence to the Midwest and provides more convenient access to one of the largest regional economies in the United States,” PAL executive vice president and COO Carlos Luis Fernandez said.
 “We know that many Filipinos and Filipino-Americans in Chicago, Illinois, and neighboring states have long looked forward to a direct and more convenient connection to the Philippines. We are proud to finally make this possible.”
 Chicago is a major hub for manufacturing, technology, healthcare and commerce, giving PAL access to business and leisure travelers across the American Midwest.
 The inaugural flight departed from Ninoy Aquino International Airport’s Terminal 1 following a send-off attended by PAL Holdings president and COO Lucio Tan III, U.S. Ambassador Lee Lipton, Tourism Secretary Bernardita Angara-Mathay and other government and aviation officials.
 The departure also marked the first use of Terminal 1’s new remote bus gate facility, part of ongoing improvements at the country’s main international gateway.
